reasons.plausibility: Boron segregation to grain boundaries is a well-known strengthening mechanism in alloys, but in this complex MM'X high-entropy system, even 0.5 at% B risks forming brittle borides that could disrupt the martensitic transformation and caloric response, making the claim of <10% caloric loss speculative without phase-diagram evidence.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and well-defined, with specific quantitative falsification criteria (30% strength increase, <10% caloric loss) and appropriate characterization methods, though the exact caloric measurement conditions (field, pressure) could be more precisely linked to the transformation.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis directly addresses the core problem of mechanical integrity versus caloric performance in a rare-earth-free system, proposing a simple, scalable metallurgical intervention that, if successful, would be highly valuable to researchers in the field.
